Appendix 8 is 'Reserved for the final version' (line 7777).

ecosystems.name: Lowland Arid
ecosystems.description: The most reduced and degraded ecosystem, with poor mapping and very little habitat left. Restoration, prioritized within the recovery footprint, is the main opportunity.
ecosystems.notes: Elevation band 0–1,000 m. Plan text lines 3620-3622.

ecosystems.name: Lowland Dry
ecosystems.description: Once the most extensive ecosystem, now down to about two percent remaining. A hotspot for rare species; restoration is the key opportunity. Better high-resolution mapping is needed to find remaining pockets of native vegetation.
ecosystems.notes: Elevation band 0–1,000 m. Plan text lines 3624-3627.

ecosystems.name: Lowland Mesic
ecosystems.description: Fragmented; areas mapped as native dominated often have heavy invasive plant understories, so 'Restore' fits much of it better than 'Initiate'. Highest original plant diversity (and likely invertebrate diversity), making targeted restoration especially valuable.
ecosystems.notes: Elevation band 0–1,000 m. Plan text lines 3629-3633.

ecosystems.name: Lowland Wet
ecosystems.description: Greatest share remaining and least invaded of the lowland ecosystems. Much good-quality habitat on partner lands is not yet ungulate-free, so 'Initiate' is the biggest opportunity.
ecosystems.notes: Elevation band 0–1,000 m. Plan text lines 3634-3637.

ecosystems.name: Montane Dry
ecosystems.description: Well represented on Hawaiʻi Island but confined to a narrow zone on East Maui, with little native-dominated vegetation left.
ecosystems.notes: Elevation band 1,000–2,000 m. Plan text lines 3639-3640. Note: Table 28 gives 56.4% remaining but Table 30 shows no Maintain/Initiate/Engage acres; flagged for DOFAW.

ecosystems.name: Montane Mesic
ecosystems.description: Largely converted to cattle pasture, so little remains, but declining ranching creates a strong restoration opportunity: many old pastures still have native trees and little invasive woody growth, making grass control plus native planting cost-effective.
ecosystems.notes: Elevation band 1,000–2,000 m; includes the small Mesic area extending into the Subalpine band. Plan text lines 3642-3645.

ecosystems.name: Montane Wet
ecosystems.description: High share of original habitat and strong plant diversity; core habitat for most remaining forest birds. 'Maintain' is the priority, though climate change may bring new threats (such as lowland-type invasive plant pressure) needing more active management.
ecosystems.notes: Elevation band 1,000–2,000 m; includes the small Wet area extending into the Subalpine band. Plan text lines 3651-3654.

ecosystems.name: Subalpine (Dry)
ecosystems.description: High quality and largely intact, mostly within Haleakalā National Park and largely ungulate-free, so 'Maintain' is the priority. Climate change is a looming risk to its narrow climatic niches.
ecosystems.notes: Elevation band 2,000–3,000 m. Plan text lines 3655-3657.

ecosystems.name: Alpine (Arid)
ecosystems.description: A tiny area at the Haleakalā summit, with less original habitat remaining than expected because of roads, parking lots and telescope facilities. Climate change is the dominant concern given its small area and species' inability to move elsewhere.
ecosystems.notes: Elevation above 3,000 m. Plan text lines 3659-3662.

ecosystems.name: Lava Pioneer
ecosystems.description: Occurs at low elevations but is more native-dominated than the other lowland ecosystems.
ecosystems.notes: Kept as a distinct ecosystem because of unique edaphic (substrate) conditions (plan lines 3566-3567). Plan text lines 3664-3665.

priorities.title: Maintain
priorities.description: Maintain managed high-quality habitat that has ungulate fences. Existing management should continue.

priorities.title: Initiate
priorities.category: Unmanaged partner lands in conservation status + high-quality habitat
priorities.description: Initiate management on lands in conservation status: identify existing native ecosystems that are in conservation status but not yet fenced. Maui Nui has extensive areas in conservation status that are not protected from ungulate damage, and some are important for both ecosystems and at-risk species recovery.

key_areas.name: Not named in plan text; southern/leeward flank of Haleakalā on Figure 27 (DOFAW to confirm)

priorities.title: Engage
priorities.description: Engage with potential partners to implement management or include areas in conservation status.
priorities.src: plan pp.99-100, lines 3959-3990; map numbers matched to names from the figure

priorities.title: Restore
priorities.category: Medium-quality habitat within ungulate-excluded areas or the recovery footprint
priorities.description: Undertake restoration of medium-quality habitats to help meet ecosystem targets for area, as well as other values, especially to support the recovery of at-risk species. Restoring areas important for species recovery, connectivity, high species diversity or climate resilience comes before areas that only add acres.
priorities.src: plan p.100, lines 3993-3995; p.97 lines 3857-3859; Table 29

special_features.name: Coastal areas
special_features.description: A varied mix of cliffs, sand dunes and wetlands.

special_features.name: Anchialine pools
special_features.description: Landlocked pools with an underground connection to the ocean through porous volcanic rock; found in only a few parts of the world and home to unique animals. Depend on groundwater-driven salinity and are vulnerable to pollution.
special_features.notes: Text (line 3579) says restricted to East Maui; Table 28 also marks Molokaʻi. Flagged for DOFAW.

special_features.name: Lava tubes
special_features.description: Cave ecosystems formed by recent volcanic activity, supporting unique fauna. Damaged by ungulates, disturbance above ground and groundwater changes.
special_features.notes: Text (lines 3580-3582) says restricted to East Maui; Table 28 also marks Molokaʻi. Flagged for DOFAW.

special_features.name: Cliffs
special_features.description: Long a refuge for unique Hawaiian flora; recent exploration with drones has found previously undocumented species.

special_features.name: Bogs
special_features.description: Localized, patchy habitats in poorly drained upland wet areas, supporting unique biota. Ungulate rooting can alter drainage and destroy rare plants.

_units: kac = thousands of acres; pct values are percent of the ecosystem's original extent (plan Tables 28 and 30).
guidelines: Protect and manage existing high-quality habitat before restoring degraded areas, especially in ecosystems with less than 40 percent of their original area remaining in high-quality habitat.
Managing high-quality areas already in conservation-oriented status can usually be done more quickly than in other areas.
Restoring areas important to species recovery, connectivity, high species diversity or climate resilience is more important than restoring areas that only add to an acreage target.
